key_insight: The paper shows that long-video QA agents need a way to recover from early search mistakes, not just zoom in on a single interval. By organizing video search like a tree with self-correction, the agent can backtrack and refine evidence localization more reliably.
problem_solved: It addresses grounded long-video question answering, where models must both answer a question and identify the short video segment that supports the answer. The key challenge is that existing agents using only coarse-to-fine cropping often get stuck after an early wrong choice and cannot recover.
method: Reframes video exploration as a tree search problem instead of a one-way narrowing process.
Introduces self-correcting agent behavior so the model can backtrack from poor evidence selections.
Uses grounded long-video QA actions to localize supporting intervals while improving robustness to early errors.
impact: This makes long-video QA agents more reliable in realistic settings where the first guess is often wrong. For practitioners, it suggests better debugging, higher answer grounding quality, and more trustworthy evidence localization in video understanding systems.
visual_elements: A tree diagram showing coarse-to-fine search paths with backtracking branches
A side-by-side comparison of single-path cropping vs self-correcting tree search
An annotated video timeline highlighting evidence intervals and incorrect crops
An agent loop icon sequence showing observe -> crop -> evaluate -> correct
paper_title: Searching Videos as Trees: Self-Correcting Agents for Grounded Long Video QA
paper_authors: Ce Zhang, Ziyang Wang, Yulu Pan, Oluwatumininu Oguntola, Pranav Wagh
